Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to England's response with the bat. The players and umpires are out to the middle. The Indian players spread out of the huddle and take their respective fielding positions. Out walk the opening pair of Phil Salt and Ben Duckett for England. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball and will kickoff the proceedings in the chase. Salt to face with a slip in waiting for him. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Well then, 158 has been the highest run chase at Pune in the T20Is, and England have a huge challenge ahead of them. Dew? Or no dew? Well, we saw a couple of groundsmen doing the mop work as soon as the innings ended, which means that there is some presence of dew on the ground. Also, the Super Soppers have been deployed out. It will be interesting to see how the Indian bowlers deal with the dew and defend their total. What would be England's approach? Will they come out and go bang bang? It is all to play for England to equalize the series. An exciting chase coming up next very shortly. Stay tuned.

India scored 41 runs in the next set of five overs losing just one wicket. Once settled well, Hardik and Dube shifted their gears quickly and runs started coming thick and fast towards the backend. This counterattack sort of disturbed the lines and lengths of the bowlers to which these two cashed on nicely. Hardik Pandya took charge of the innings, assertively batting his way to a half-century and pushing the team's score deeper into a competitive range before perishing. And then, it was Jamie Overton who wrapped up things nicely in the backend and took a few quick wickets to peg India back. But, Dube stuck to his aggressive style and squeezed out a few lusty blows as well, scoring a fifty of his own too.

That little push from Abhishek and Rinku did help India increase the scoring rate and provided some breathing room for the others to come. The English pacers continued to test the batters with those well-directed short ones, while Adil Rashid displayed the mastery of his variations to slow things down. As a result, India wasn't allowed to run away and found themselves 72/4 at the halfway mark. However, Shivam Dube tried to keep the scoring rate at a brisk pace and did play some powerful shots to the boundary, and he was ably helped by Hardik Pandya who played second-fiddle to him.

However, Abhishek Sharma stood tall against the early devastation, batting with extraordinary flair. He defied the mounting pressure with a stunning display of strokeplay during the powerplay, unleashing a series of glorious shots that breathed life into India's innings. Rinku Singh proved an able ally, joining Sharma in a calculated counterattack that gradually restored the team's momentum. But it was soon halted by the vastly experienced Adil Rashid who struck gold in his first over.

It was the first time that India was asked to set the total in this series which of course brought new challenges ahead of them and were rocked badly pretty early into the innings. Bowling thunderbolts, Saqib Mahmood transformed India's batting dreams into a nightmare, reducing them to a mere 12/3 in a breathtaking early onslaught. Stepping into Mark Wood's formidable shoes, Mahmood delivered a fiery spell, leaving Sanju Samson, Suryakumar Yadav, and Tilak Varma scrambling against his express pace.

A strong finish from England and Jamie Overton, just 3 runs from the last over along with three wickets as well. But, India managed to score 68 runs off the last five overs, thanks to Hardik and Dube's counterpunch. It was again England's fiery pace attack versus the Indian batters and the latter again looked a bit vulnerable in the beginning on a surface that offered good bounce and pace.

OUT! RUN OUT! Incredible work from Jos Buttler! Outstanding last over from Jamie Overton. The 20th over goes for just 3 runs. Overton bangs it into the deck, around off, Shivam Dube fails to get on top of it and flat bats it towards long on. He takes the first one and turns around quickly for the second run. Jos Buttler swoops in and gets to the ball. Picks it up cleanly and fires in a throw on the bounce at the batting end. He knocks the stumps down and the third umpire is called into action. The replays show that Dube is short of his crease despite the stretch. So, just 1 run from the last ball and India will finish on 181!

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.3: Adil Rashid to Shivam Dube, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shivam Dube is in at number 6.

OUT! TAKEN! Four and out for Abhishek against Rashid! The leggie strikes with his 2nd ball. This is slower through the air, around off, Abhishek Sharma reaches out in front and gets down on a knee for the slog sweep. Fails to get the elevation and picks out the man in the deep to perfection. Hits it flat and straight down the throat of Jacob Bethell at deep mid-wicket. Just as the partnership was starting to flourish, India have been pegged back. They are 57/4 now as Abhishek Sharma departs for a brisk 29 (19).
Commentary.Howout: c Jacob Bethell b Adil Rashid
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Adil Rashid to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! c Jacob Bethell b Adil Rashid.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Rashid is greeted with a boundary! This is pushed through, on a length, on off, Abhishek Sharma extends his hands into the shot and cracks the drive to the right of cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Adil Rashid to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Spin from the other end? Indeed. Here's Adil Rashid. He replaces Jamie Overton.

FOUR! Gets it through! Slightly fuller, on off, Rinku Singh leans into the shot and drives it to the right of the man at cover inside the ring. He also beats the diving fielder in the deep to his left to pick up a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Jamie Overton to Rinku Singh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! This skids through, on a back of a length, Rinku Singh stays leg side of the ball and tries to run it down to deep third but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Jamie Overton to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length, on off, Abhishek Sharma tries to pull it towards cow corner but ends up hitting it straighter towards long on. He mistimes the shot and that helps him in a way as the ball drops well short of Harry Brook at long on. A single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Jamie Overton to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower and going across the left-hander, on the fuller side, Abhishek Sharma reaches out and eases it towards backward point where Ben Duckett tumbles to his right and prevents the single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Jamie Overton to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling across, on a length, Rinku Singh angles the bat face and dabs it towards backward point where Ben Duckett fumbles and concedes a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Jamie Overton to Rinku Singh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Attacking the stumps, full in length, firmly driven to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Jamie Overton to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Jamie Overton is introduced into the attack now. He replaces Brydon Carse.

On off and middle, on a back of a length, Rinku Singh makes room and dances down the track to force it through the off side. Ends up chopping it down in front of point for one. At the end of the Powerplay, India are 47/3.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Saqib Mahmood to Rinku Singh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Nonchalantly done! This is on a shortish length, over off and middle, Rinku Singh picks up the length early and presses back. Uses his wrists to play the pick-up shot over deep backward square leg for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Saqib Mahmood to Rinku Singh, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Better line, on top of off, on a short of a length, Rinku Singh steers it straight to Jofra Archer at short third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Saqib Mahmood to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit too straight again, on the pads, on a hard length, Abhishek Sharma tucks it wide of backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length, on the pads, Abhishek Sharma lets the ball come to him and flicks it through mid-wicket. Calls for two immediately and he gets it with ease.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length, on off, Abhishek Sharma hangs back and glides it towards short third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Too full and around off, Rinku Singh gets forward and drives it straight to short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Brydon Carse to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dug in short and on the stumps, Rinku Singh ducks underneath it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Brydon Carse to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shot! Back of a length, on the middle and leg, Rinku Singh charges down the track again and heaves it to deep mid-wicket for a cracking boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Brydon Carse to Rinku Singh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: TOP EDGE AND FOUR! Some intent from Rinku Singh! Buttler won't mind this one bit! A well-directed short-pitched delivery, on the bodyline, nipping away, Rinku Singh gives the bowler the charge and tries to pull but the top-edge flies the ball over the slips for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Brydon Carse to Rinku Singh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Aims the blockhole, and gets the yorker correct, on off, Rinku Singh squats and carves it out to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Brydon Carse to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Brydon Carse comes into the attack now, replacing Jofra Archer! Begins with a good-length delivery, outside off, Abhishek Sharma cuts it square to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Brydon Carse to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Brydon Carse comes into the attack as the first change.

BEATEN! Just a yard ahead of the short length, and over the top of off, nipping away a shy bit. Rinku Singh stays rooted in his crease and tries to nudge it around the corner but gets beaten by the express pace. The ball passes above his angled bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Saqib Mahmood to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 137.7 kph, on a hard length, outside off, Abhishek Sharma plays it late and hits it to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Goodness me, that is a shot of high quality! Pitched-up delivery, in the arc, on off, Abhishek Sharma gets forward, hits it through the line and finds the gap between cover and point for a cracking boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off, slanting away on a length, Abhishek Sharma slashes and misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Timing! Length-delivery, outside off, Abhishek Sharma stands tall and punches it through the gap between cover and mid off for a boundary. The cover fielder tries to stop it with the dive to his left but the ball evades him and runs to the boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, fairly outside off, Abhishek Sharma shuffles and covers the stumps, looks to loft it over the bowler's head but misses as the ball nips away from him.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Saqib Mahmood to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good gas from Archer! Short and on the bodyline, Rinku dodges under it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Jofra Archer to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Now that is a good shot from Rinku! Seam-up, full and on middle, Rinku Singh shimmies down the track and offers himself some room, opens his arms, and slaps it past covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Jofra Archer to Rinku Singh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and outside off, Rinku Singh jabs it away towards point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Jofra Archer to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling on the pads on a fuller length, Abhishek Sharma misses to flick and the ball deflects off his front pad to the keeper where Salt fumbles a bit and allows the batters to cross over for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off, Rinku Singh hops on the back foot and gets a thick outside edge that runs down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Jofra Archer to Rinku Singh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and outside off, Abhishek gets across to the other end after playing it with soft hands to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rinku Singh walks out to bat with India in early strife.

OUT! CAUGHT! The Pune crowd is in absolute silence now as SKY departs on a four-ball duck! India in deep, deep trouble! Saqib Mahmood stays over the stumps and spears the ball on the fullish length, angling into the middle and leg stump channel. Suryakumar Yadav stays in the crease and looks to flick it in the mid on and mid-wicket gap, but hits it off the higher part of the bat and the bat twists in his hands at the point of contact. Hence, the ball just chips off the willow and goes parallel to the ground and Brydon Carse at short mid on takes a simple catch. England are thrilled to bits and the Indian skipper cannot believe it!
Commentary.Howout: c Brydon Carse b Saqib Mahmood
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Saqib Mahmood to Suryakumar Yadav, OUT! c Brydon Carse b Saqib Mahmood.

Commentary.Commentary: Aims the sticks, does Saqib, on a fullish length, on middle, Suryakumar Yadav blocks it in front.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Saqib Mahmood to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the back of a length, on top of off, at 135.9 kph, Suryakumar Yadav gets on the back foot and stabs it on the surface.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Saqib Mahmood to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and at 138.6 kph, full and around off, Suryakumar Yadav works it straight to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Saqib Mahmood to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The Indian skipper, Suryakumar Yadav walks out to face the hat-trick ball. Two slips and a short leg in place.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN AGAIN! Saqib Mahmood is on a HAT-TRICK! India are in early trouble and Tilak Varma departs for a golden duck! Saqib fires in a fuller-length delivery and keeps it just around off. It lands and skids through quickly as Tilak Varma charges down the track to give it a whack over the in-field. But ends up getting a thickish outside edge that flies straight behind and dips ahead of Jofra Archer at deep third. Archer does well, gets low on his haunches and takes a fine catch to his right. India are 12/2 now.
Commentary.Howout: c Jofra Archer b Saqib Mahmood
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Saqib Mahmood to Tilak Varma, OUT! c Jofra Archer b Saqib Mahmood.

Commentary.Commentary: Tilak Varma walks in at number 3.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! And again, the short ball becomes the nemesis for Sanju Samson as he departs on a cheap score! England are overjoyed and rightly so and Saqib Mahmood makes an impact right away! Saqib steams in from over the pegs and bangs it into the surface, short and on the bodyline of the right-hander, Sanju Samson is rushed and the ball gets a bit heavy on him as well. He does go through the shot and pulls it aerially, looking to clear the square leg fielder, but doesn't get the timing right and the ball sails straight down the throat of Brydon Carse in the deep.
Commentary.Howout: c Brydon Carse b Saqib Mahmood
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Saqib Mahmood to Sanju Samson, OUT! c Brydon Carse b Saqib Mahmood.

Commentary.Commentary: Brought into the side for Mark Wood, Saqib Mahmood will operate from the other end.

FOUR! A positive start for Abhishek Sharma and India! 12 runs off the opening over! Almost a half-tracker slightly around off, Abhishek stays leg side of the ball and smashes it past mid off for a cracking boundary. The fielder gives it a chase to the ropes but the ball wins the race.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Wow! What a beautiful shot! Back of a length, just outside off, Abhishek Sharma gets everything he desires - length, width and height. Climbs on the ball and just helps it behind deep backward point for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! At 143.6 kph, around off on a fullish length, Abhishek Sharma shimmies down the track to create room and tries to slash it away but misses and the ball passes above his angled bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a good length, on off, Abhishek Sharma climbs on the bounce and knocks it to the point region where Duckett again does well to intercept the ball to his left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Samson is off the mark now! First runs off the bat! Could have been a boundary but Ben Duckett does an excellent job in the inner ring! Back of a length, outside off, Sanju Samson stays back and cuts it nicely to pierce the point region but Duckett puts in a sharp dive to his right and half-stops it. Parries the ball to the cover region and the batters cross over for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! He will have to reload that one again! Inswinger, going way down leg on a length. Wide given!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: A slip in place for Archer along with a leg gully! He starts on the money! Gets a good tail back into the batter, from off, on a hard length, Sanju Samson hops across to glance it away but gets a deflection off his gloves onto the thigh pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going here in Pune. Jos Buttler leads his troops out to the centre. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson to open the innings for India. Jofra Archer will start with the new ball for England. Archer to Samson first up. A slip and a leg gully in place. Here we go!

The Indian captain, Suryakumar Yadav, says that the team is focused on playing a good brand of cricket and sticking to the basics. He mentions that they have come into this game fresh after the defeat and are eager to put on a good show. Speaking about the conditions, he notes that the pitch is a little on the drier side and hopes that dew doesn’t play a big role, allowing them to defend a total effectively. Informs that they have made three changes - Arshdeep Singh comes in for Mohammed Shami, Rinku Singh is fit and replaces Dhruv Jurel and Shivam Dube comes in for Washington Sundar.

The captain of England, Jos Buttler says that the atmosphere feels great and the series is nicely set up as well. Mentions he is happy with the performance and also accepts that they do have a few areas of improvement. About the pitch, he shares that he is a little bit unsure how the dew will play. Informs two changes in the side - Saqib Mahmood and Jacob Bethell come in the mix for Mark Wood and Jamie Smith respectively.

England (Playing XI) - Ben Duckett, Phil Salt (WK), Jos Buttler (C), Harry Brook, Liam Livingstone, Jacob Bethell (In for Jamie Smith), Jamie Overton, Brydon Carse, Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid, Saqib Mahmood (In for Mark Wood).

India (Playing XI) - Sanju Samson (WK), Abhishek Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya, Rinku Singh (In for Dhruv Jurel), Shivam Dube (In for Washington Sundar), Axar Patel, Ravi Bishnoi, Arshdeep Singh (In for Mohammed Shami), Varun Chakravarthy.
TOSS - England have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Nick Knight and Murali Kartik are out in the middle. Kartik points out that a strong breeze is blowing across the ground. Informs that the square boundaries are 65 and 64 meters, while the straight hit measures 75 meters. Nick adds that the surface consists of 60 percent red soil and 40 percent black soil, which means there will be good carry and bounce, suiting England. Adds that the presence of dead grass, which has been rolled in, suggests that the pitch is pretty dry with some cracks. He expects pace-on deliveries to travel well, but there is something in it for both pacers and spinners, especially for those who take the pace off the ball.

The Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium of Pune presents an intriguing paradox. While the first innings have seen towering totals, with 206 being the benchmark, the chase narrative tells a different story. The highest successful pursuit here stands at a modest 158, coincidentally set in a 2012 clash between these very teams. The traditional black-soil wicket at Pune, with its historical fondness for spin bowling, adds another fascinating dimension to today's team selections. As both sides ponder their combinations for this crucial encounter, do stick around for the toss and team updates flashing on your screens shortly.

Breaking from the injury front, there's positive news in the Indian camp as Rinku Singh has shaken off his back spasms and returns to the selection pool, potentially displacing Dhruv Jurel or triggering other lineup changes. Meanwhile, England faces a setback with Jamie Smith's calf strain from the previous encounter, possibly paving the way for Jacob Bethell's return, a move that would bolster their spin options alongside Rashid and Livingstone.

England, buoyed by their Rajkot triumph, face what essentially amounts to two consecutive must-win games to clinch the series. Jos Buttler has been in his characteristic aggressive form, finding able support from Ben Duckett and Liam Livingstone. However, concerns linger over Phil Salt's performance, as he's yet to breach double figures in the series. Similarly, Harry Brook's form has been below par, leaving England with their own batting conundrums to solve. England’s pacers have effectively troubled the Indian batters hitting those hit-the-deck-hard lengths and have benefited largely from them and are expected to continue with this tactic in Pune as well.

While India maintains their series lead, the Rajkot defeat exposed some significant concerns, particularly in their batting department. The form of key players remains a worry, notably Sanju Samson and captain Suryakumar Yadav, with SKY managing just one fifty-plus score in his last ten T20I appearances, a stark contrast to his usual explosive standards. However, the emergence of Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma has helped paper over these cracks, while Hardik Pandya continues to prove his worth as an all-rounder. In the bowling department, Varun Chakravarthy has been exceptional, already claiming a five-wicket haul in this series.

Cricket's age-old battle between pace and spin has taken center stage in this series, with both teams wielding their preferred weapons to devastating effect. While India's spinners have kept England's batters in a constant puzzle, the visitors' pace battery has responded with equal venom, particularly showcased in their Rajkot triumph. The return of Mohammed Shami has added extra teeth to India's pace resources, complemented by Arshdeep Singh's impressive showings. Not to be outdone in the spin department, England's Adil Rashid has proven to be a crucial weapon, especially during those crucial middle overs. Boy, it is neck and neck, isn’t it?

Kolkata, check. Chennai, done. Rajkot, just a few moons behind. The caravan now moves to the city beloved known as the ‘Queen of the Deccan’ in this 5-match series between India and England, and things have started to heat up in a true sense as the series stands well-poised 2-1 in favor of India. However, with England breaching Rajkot, the momentum lies with the visitors. On that note, we extend our warm welcome to the coverage of the 4th and the penultimate T20I as both teams are again ready to trade some tough punches in Pune.
... MATCH DAY ...

England have finally arrived in India, and they’ve done it in style! After two tough losses, they delivered a statement win in Rajkot to keep the T20I series alive. They came close in Chennai too, only to be denied by Tilak Varma’s sensational knock. Earlier, it was Abhishek Sharma’s clean striking that stole the show in Kolkata, but his opening partner Sanju Samson is yet to make his mark. Skipper Suryakumar Yadav, known for his explosive batting, will also be eager to stamp his authority as India aim to wrap up the series. Gautam Gambhir and SKY have placed their faith in all-rounders, and so far, it has paid off. Axar Patel and Washington Sundar provide solid spin options, while Hardik Pandya not only adds firepower to the batting but also plays the role of a reliable second pacer. Dhruv Jurel’s presence at No. 8 gives them incredible depth. But the real star with the ball has been Varun Chakravarthy. The mystery spinner has bagged 10 wickets in just three matches, including a stunning five-wicket haul in the last game - an effort that won him the Player of the Match award despite India’s defeat. Ravi Bishnoi has also chipped in well, but India's strategy of playing just one specialist pacer could be reconsidered. If they want extra firepower, they might bring in Ramandeep Singh, Shivam Dube, or even Rinku Singh - depending on his fitness. Meanwhile, England will feel they have the momentum now. Captain Jos Buttler has been leading from the front with the bat, and in the last game, he finally got much-needed support from Ben Duckett and Liam Livingstone. The explosive Phil Salt has been quiet so far, but is he saving his best for the last two games? England certainly hope so. The visitors’ bowling attack looks sharp, with the express pace of Jofra Archer and Mark Wood keeping the Indian batters on their toes. Brydon Carse and Jamie Overton have provided useful variations, while the ever-reliable Adil Rashid, along with Livingstone’s ability to mix up off-breaks and leg-breaks, gives England a strong spin department. With the series now poised at 2-1, England will be hungry to level things up and take it to a decider. Can they pull off another win, or will India bounce back and seal the series with a game to spare? Buckle up - this battle is far from over!
